evidence_set: The national programme on Substance Abuse Deaths (np-SAD), fed by coroners, supplied local performance figures under a wider definition than the UK Drug Strategy definition, also counting deaths in which psychoactive substances were implicated (with or without a post-mortem), deaths with a history of drug use problems and deaths with controlled drugs present at post-mortem. Of the 70 deaths np-SAD reported for Liverpool (57 deaths in 2004 and 28 inquests in January to June 2005, duplicates removed), np-SAD placed 38 in its category for people with a known history of problem drug use, 21 outside it and 11 as unknown; 45 were deaths from drug toxicity (prescribed drugs included) and 55 were of Liverpool residents. Editors' arithmetic: 25 of the 70 were not deaths from drug toxicity and 15 were not Liverpool residents.
